front: Block vs file vs object storage?
back: Block: raw disk for one machine. File: shared paths over NFS/SMB. Object: flat key → object over HTTP.
Near-unlimited scale and durability; no in-place updates; higher latency per request.
A bucket holds objects; each object is bytes + metadata under a unique key.
Just key prefixes; the namespace is flat.
Strong read-after-write for all operations since December 2020.

front: Files in the database: why not?
back: Expensive storage, slow backups and replicas, cache pollution, and serving through app servers.
Bytes in object storage, metadata (key, owner, size) in the database.
A URL signed by your service allowing one operation on one object until it expires.
Parts 5 MB–5 GB, up to 10,000 parts, objects up to 5 TB; single PUT max 5 GB.
Automatically moves or deletes objects by age or prefix.
Retrieval fees, minimum storage durations, slow archive restores.
Bucket as private origin, CDN at the edge, versioned keys with long cache lifetimes.
